successors.name: Habsburg monarchy
successors.text: the Habsburg hereditary lands, as Cliopatria's Habsburg Monarchy row draws them from 1516

rulers.name: Rudolf I
rulers.title: Count of Habsburg (1239-1291); King of the Romans from 1273

rulers.name: Albert I
rulers.title: Duke of Austria (from 1282); Holy Roman Emperor 1298-1308

rulers.name: Frederick the Fair
rulers.title: Duke of Austria and Styria, with Leopold I

rulers.name: Albert II
rulers.title: Duke of Austria and Styria; of Further Austria from 1326; Carinthia after 1335

rulers.name: Albert V (Albert II of Germany)
rulers.title: Duke of Austria; king of Hungary and of the Romans from 1437-1438

rulers.name: Ladislaus the Posthumous
rulers.title: Duke of Austria; king of Hungary and Bohemia

rulers.name: Frederick III

rulers.title: King of the Romans (Germany) after 1493; emperor 1508-1519

ledger.x: 1260: the Habsburg counts hold their home lands around Habsburg Castle in the Aargau.
1264: Rudolf seizes the Kyburg estates.
1276: the Habsburgs take Vienna as their seat.
1276: Ottokar II of Bohemia gives up Austria and its neighbours to Rudolf.
December 1282: Rudolf makes Austria and Styria hereditary duchies of his house.
1286: Carinthia goes to Count Meinhard.
1311: the Habsburgs take over Savinja.
1335: Carinthia and Carniola fall to the Habsburgs.
1363: Margaret Maultasch leaves Tyrol to Rudolf IV of Austria.
1374: the Habsburgs reach Istria.
25 September 1379: the Treaty of Neuberg divides the Habsburg lands between two lines.
1382: Trieste comes to the Habsburgs.
1402: about 1,300 km2 appear in the shape.
1415: the Swiss conquer the Aargau.
December 1437: Albert V becomes king of Hungary.
27 October 1439: Albert dies at Neszmely; his reign as king of Hungary and of the Romans ends, and Ladislaus the Posthumous succeeds as duke of Austria.
29 January 1453: the Hungarian Diet recognises Ladislaus.
28 October 1453: Ladislaus is crowned king of Bohemia at Prague.
23 November 1457: Ladislaus dies at Prague and the union of Hungary with the Habsburg house ends; Matthias Corvinus is elected about two months later.
23 November 1457: Ladislaus dies and Bohemia leaves the union; 'George of Poděbrady was elected king of Bohemia on 3 March 1458'.
1460: the Swiss take the Thurgau.
1469: Sigismund pawns Further Austria to Charles the Bold.
1474: the Burgundian pawn of Further Austria ends ('From 1469 to 1474').
1477: Matthias Corvinus invades Lower Austria.
August 1477: Maximilian marries Mary of Burgundy while France holds her lands.
1 December 1477: peace between Matthias and Frederick III ('which was signed on 1 December 1477'); Frederick confirms Matthias as ruler of Bohemia.
1481: Matthias seizes Sankt Polten and Mautern.
1482: the Burgundian Netherlands pass to the Habsburgs.
23 December 1482: the Treaty of Arras.
1485: the Hungarian campaign turns into an occupation of Lower Austria.
1485: the Black Army takes Vienna.
1487: Cliopatria moves the Burgundian Netherlands from the House of Habsburg row to its Habsburg Monarchy row (1487-1506).
1490: Tyrol and Further Austria are reunited under Maximilian.
August 1490: Vienna is recovered.
1500: the Gorizia inheritance.
30 July 1505: Maximilian takes the Kufstein territory.
1507: the Burgundian lands are back in the House row.
1515: Cliopatria's House of Habsburg row ends; its Habsburg Monarchy row carries the hereditary lands from 1516.

wars.name: Rudolf I's war with Ottokar II of Bohemia (Battle on the Marchfeld)
wars.outcome: War declared June 1276; in November 1276 Ottokar cedes the four provinces to royal administration; on 26 August 1278 Ottokar is defeated and killed at the Battle on the Marchfeld (paraphrased).

wars.name: Habsburg wars with the Swiss (Morgarten, Sempach, Naefels, the Aargau)
wars.outcome: Swiss victories over the Habsburgs at Morgarten (1315), Sempach (1386) and Naefels (1388); the Swiss conquer the Aargau in 1415 and the Thurgau in 1460.

wars.name: Austrian-Hungarian War (1477-1488)
wars.outcome: Hungarian victory: the Black Army captures Vienna (1485) and Wiener Neustadt (1487); 'In 1490, Matthias' unexpected death led to a reversal of his gains' and the Peace of Pressburg (1491) arranged the return of the conquests.

wars.name: War of the Burgundian Succession
wars.outcome: France annexes the Duchy of Burgundy and several other territories; the Treaty of Arras (23 December 1482) leaves Artois and Franche-Comte with France as Margaret's dowry; the Treaty of Senlis (1493) returns them to Philip the Handsome.

wars.name: War of the Succession of Landshut
wars.outcome: Victory of Bavaria-Munich; Maximilian arbitrates at Cologne on 30 July 1505 and keeps the Kufstein territory for the County of Tyrol; Palatinate-Neuburg is created for the heirs of Bavaria-Landshut.

wars.name: Maximilian I's war on Venice (League of Cambrai)
wars.outcome: 'One particularly humiliating campaign occurred in 1508,' when Maximilian attacked Venice and was blocked; 'He acknowledged French control of Milan in 1515.'

certainty.note: A dynasty's scattered holdings (Aargau, Alsace, Austria, Tyrol, the Istrian outposts); the dukedoms of Austria and Styria have defined edges but the pages give no surveyed lines.
The French frontier of the Burgundian lands is treaty-fixed (Arras, 23 December 1482; Senlis, 1493) and could be drawn sharp; every other frontier stays soft.
